data.body:
Dependency edges created across the 27 children from file-impact overlap analysis (30 depends_on edges).

Only 5/27 children declared file_impact, so next-batch's conflict-aware batching could not see these collisions; footprints were derived from each ticket's file:line-cited description.

Layering (verified acyclic, graphlib topological sort):
  L0 point fixes: 176d 2d1c 2e16 723f 7504 7be3 8537 9ce8 ae96 c9c6 d064 da31 e63c
  L1: 1de3 3803 47e9 4fc1   L2: 4b94 8efe f0ff fc0c   L3: 373f 8a31 ad16   L4: 0743 da4c   L5: ab77

Rationale per class:
- Shared-file serialization: 3803+723f and 4fc1 on _commands/txn.py; 1de3+723f on adapters/jira/backend.py; 47e9+f0ff+8efe on .github/workflows/_build-and-test.yml; 47e9+f0ff+ae96 on scripts/.
- Stated carve-outs: fc0c depends on 7504/3803/c9c6 (its AC forbids folding those three defects in); 8a31 depends on f0ff (its text: sequence after, the envelope exit_code field needs the complete vocabulary).
- Comment triage 373f blankets src/rebar (439 files), so it depends on all 15 point fixes in its scope — triage must read final code, not code about to change.
- The six shards all append .joe-janitor/tools.md and add ADRs, so they are chained: 9ce8 -> 4fc1 -> 4b94 -> ad16 -> da4c -> ab77.
- 0743 (ADR renumbering) is pinned last behind 373f/1de3/8537, per the epic plan-review advisory that it races with children that amend or create ADRs by number.

Note: 0743 shows as L4 but effectively lands after L5 — it blocks on 373f CLOSING, and the open-children guard holds 373f until ab77 closes.
